name: Altea
title: Holidays in Altea
intro: A whitewashed hill town on the Costa Blanca, crowned by a blue-domed church, with a pebble seafront and Benidorm's beaches next door. Here's what Altea is like, when to go and how long to stay.
image_alt: The blue-and-white domes and bell tower of Altea's church
facts_note: The EU is bringing in new entry checks, so check the rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: May, June, September and October are ideal, warm with a pleasant sea. July and August are hot and busy. Winter is mild and sunny, with many visitors from northern Europe.

things.name: Old town
things.blurb: Steep white lanes up to the blue-and-white domed church and its viewpoint.

things.name: Seafront promenade
things.blurb: A long pebble beach lined with cafés and restaurants.

things.name: Serra Gelada
things.blurb: A cliff walk to a lighthouse between Altea and Benidorm.

things.name: Algar waterfalls
things.blurb: Turquoise pools and falls for swimming, 25 minutes inland.

things.name: Guadalest
things.blurb: A tiny castle village perched on a rock above a reservoir.

things.name: Benidorm beaches
things.blurb: Long sandy beaches and theme parks next door.

faqs.question: Is Altea worth visiting?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's one of the prettiest towns on the Costa Blanca, with an arty old town and a calmer feel than nearby Benidorm.

faqs.question: Does Altea have a sandy beach?
faqs.answer: Altea's beaches are mostly pebbles. For sand, head to Albir or Benidorm, a short drive away.

faqs.question: How do you get to Altea?
faqs.answer: Fly into Alicante, which has many direct flights from the UK, then drive or take the bus or tram, about an hour.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Altea?
faqs.answer: May, June, September and October, around 22 to 29°C.

faqs.question: How many nights do you need in Altea?
faqs.answer: A week gives time for the old town, the beaches, the waterfalls and Guadalest.
